title: Positivity of a family size bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $varepsilon$ be rational with $0<varepsilon\le\tfrac12$, let $M$ be a natural number, and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. If $|\mathcal F|\le M$ and the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ indexed by subsets outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $varepsilon/4$, then $M>0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$
Fourier weight outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $varepsilon/4$
